signatures.name: utilitarian_preference
signatures.description: When numbers differ, agents prefer to save the larger group. Awad et al. 2018 (Nature) global aggregate.
signatures.bias_rationale: A moral preference whose normative status is contested, not a capacity.

signatures.name: age_preference_save_young
signatures.description: Agents prefer to save the young over the elderly. Awad et al. 2018 global aggregate.
signatures.bias_rationale: Age-based triage is a human preference with no agreed normative standing.

signatures.name: species_preference_save_human
signatures.description: Agents prefer to save humans over pets. The largest single-factor effect in the Moral Machine global data.
signatures.bias_rationale: A human-centric preference, not a capacity.

signatures.name: legality_preference_save_lawful
signatures.description: When legality differs, agents prefer to save the lawful pedestrians (kill the jaywalkers). Awad et al. 2018 global aggregate ~0.61 — mild but reliable.
signatures.bias_rationale: Punishing jaywalking with death is a preference, not a capacity.

_notes.intervention_aversion: Removed in v1.2.1. The task allocates 4 intervention trials; against a chance level of 0.5 the best attainable exact-binomial p is 0.0625, so no behaviour could ever clear threshold_p=0.05. It reported untestable in all 50 archived sessions (40 panel + 10 floor) and so was already excluded from every L3 denominator — removal changes no reported number. Restore it only alongside a trials_per_dimension.intervention count with power.
